lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Nadège, it's Jean. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Jean. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not great. My knees have been bothering me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Come on, you can find 10 minutes.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already bought new sneakers.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, my diabetes is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to walk 15 minutes on 5 days. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Invites check-in on how she is
Reports knee discomfort, a minor barrier
Warns of health consequences without permission
Shared goal with family; enjoys walking; not reflected
Asks how she wants to handle walking
Reframes as ongoing exploration, softens resistance
Asks whether she tried the mall
Reports trying a step toward activity
Adds meaning about starting small and sticking with it
Reminder on fridge as a step
Plans to involve son for support
Requests later time due to appointment

flags.reason: Warns of health decline without permission; confrontational rather than collaborative.
'Come on, you can find 10 minutes' pushes after participant committed; pressure, not partnership.
'You need to walk every day, no excuses' is a directive that ignores her stated barriers and ambivalence.
Participant reports sharing goal with family and enjoying the idea; coach did not reflect or affirm it.

score.summary: The coach used useful open questions and ended with a clear, summarized goal that the participant confirmed, including barrier planning. However, three persuading statements (lines 10, 16, 22) pushed against the participant's ambivalence, and her change talk at line 21 went unreflected.
strengths: Line 5 opens with an open question about how she is really doing, inviting honest disclosure.
Line 40 summarizes the agreed plan and checks accuracy, and line 41 confirms it.
Line 38 explores barriers openly, and line 39 leads to a concrete support plan with her son.
coaching_tips: Replace line 22's 'no excuses' directive with a reflection, e.g., 'Walking every day feels like a lot right now.'
Reflect the change talk in line 21 ('You told your family and found you like the idea') to build momentum.
Ask permission before advice, as done in line 18, and avoid warnings like line 10; try 'What worries you most about your health right now?'
Use complex reflections more, such as line 29, to explore ambivalence rather than pressing for commitment after line 15.
